parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: A column of dates from a marked date table that represents the current period to shift back one year.
parameters.examNote: Must be from a date table marked as a date table. The table must be contiguous with no date gaps, otherwise the shifted period may not align correctly.

returnType: Table (a single-column table of dates corresponding to the same period one year prior)
summary: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns a table of dates representing the equivalent period exactly one year ago. It is used inside CALCULATE to create prior-year comparison measures such as Last Year Sales or Year-over-Year growth. Like all time intelligence functions, it requires a properly marked, continuous date table and is always used as a CALCULATE filter argument.

examples.label: Prior year sales comparison
examples.explanation: For Q1 2024 (January–March 2024), SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR returns January–March 2023. CALCULATE then sums Sales for that prior-year period, returning 1000.

examples.label: Year-over-year growth percentage
examples.expression: YoY Growth % = DIVIDE([Total Sales] - [Sales LY], [Sales LY], 0)
examples.explanation: By subtracting last year's sales from current and dividing by last year, you get the percentage change. DIVIDE is used here to safely handle cases where [Sales LY] is zero or blank.

steps: Current filter context has a date range (e.g., March 2024)
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR shifts every date in that range back exactly 12 months
The resulting date table covers March 2023
CALCULATE replaces the current date filter with this prior-year date set
The expression is evaluated for the prior-year period

commonTraps: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR requires a contiguous, gap-free date table. If dates are missing, the shifted period may not map correctly and results become unreliable.
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is a table function used inside CALCULATE. It cannot be used standalone as a measure.
For shifting periods other than exactly one year (e.g., 3 months or 2 years), use DATEADD instead — SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is fixed at exactly -1 year.

sqlEquivalent.expression: WHERE Date BETWEEN DATEADD(year, -1, PeriodStart) AND DATEADD(year, -1, PeriodEnd)
sqlEquivalent.note: SQL achieves this by manually offsetting the WHERE clause date boundaries by one year. SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR automatically computes the prior-year equivalent of whatever period is in the current filter context, eliminating hardcoded date boundaries.
